title: Senescent Cells: Emerging Targets for Human Aging and Age-Related Diseases - ScienceDirect
abstract:
New studies have illustrated the promising feasibility and safety to selectively ablate senescent cells from tissues, a therapeutic modality that holds potential for treating multiple chronic pathologies and extending human healthspan.
New studies have illustrated the promising feasibility and safety to selectively ablate senescent cells from tissues, a therapeutic modality that holds potential for treating multiple chronic pathologies and extending human healthspan. Here, we review molecular links between cellular senescence and age-associated complications and highlight novel therapeutic avenues that may be exploited to target senescent cells in future geriatric medicine.
Targeted elimination of senescent cells has emerged as a promising therapeutic solution to ameliorate tissue damage and promote repair and regeneration.
In the scope of clinical medicine, advances that identify key biochemical pathways, specifically those differentiating senescent cells from their proliferating counterparts, would positively affect pathological and aging processes. Aging is a major risk factor for numerous human pathologies, including cardiovascular, metabolic, musculoskeletal, and neurodegenerative conditions and various malignancies. While our understanding of aging is far from complete, recent advances suggest that targeting fundamental aging processes can delay, prevent, or alleviate age-related disorders.
